**Daily Devotional**

**June 4**

*2 This only would I learn of you, Received ye the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith? 3 Are ye so foolish? having begun in the Spirit, are ye now made perfect by the flesh? (Galatians 3:2-3 KJV)*

Paul has been telling the Galatians that the way they received Christ is the same way they should continue in their walk with the Lord. The Word of God makes it clear that we are saved by Faith in the Grace of God (Ephesians 2:8) through our Savior Jesus Christ. In Paul’s day there were those Jews that were trying to get the Galatians to also abide by all the Law of Moses, by keeping the feast days, circumcision, and all the rules and regulations of the Jews. The shame of it is that religion today is doing the same sort of thing. They don’t teach all the old rules of the Jews, but they still teach that after you are saved, you have to tithe, go to church, read your bible, and all their other duties, for God to answer your prayers and move in your life. That is just not so. God does not respond to your works, but only to your faith in Christ (Galatians 2:16), and God loves you the same whether you do all the things religion tells you to do, or not.

Your works do not make God respond to you, but your living holy will affect your love for God, and make your heart to become sensitive to God, whereas your unholy living will make your heart become hard towards God, and can eventually make you reject your salvation, so you don’t want to live in sin. Sin also opens the door to the devil (John 10:10) to come in with sickness, poverty, and all kinds of evil (Romans 6:16), so a holy life needs to be led by all Christians (1 Peter 1:15). Thank you Jesus!

Question: If Doom and Doom 2 didn't have disappearing bodies, why does almost every first person shooter in these days have disappearing bodies?

Doom is a 2D game with enemies occupying an XY coordinate portrayed by a static 2D sprite.

Modern games have enemies with full 3D textured models (often with all kinds of mapping, shading and tesselation) that are then rag-dolled over the environment with a physics engine. The memory requirements are quite higher in this scenario.
( Also a room filled to the brim with corpses isn't great for gameplay... )
Depends on your perspective. It'd help show where you've already been.

Key word being "help". Good level design is appreciated, but the complete package is what makes it a good experience.

Then they should better optimise the models/geometry/physics handling. I'm tired of this excuse. We can have both good looking games as well as games that have thousands of rendered entities at the same time.

To draw a comparison, Halo Reach's Magnum - a magazine-fed pistol, the smallest weapon in the game - has more polygons than an entire marine model from Halo 3. It's ridiculous. We shouldn't be shooting for "DURR MOST POLYGONS IN SCENE" and instead go for how many actors can move around and interact with the player's character. I want density, not pointless detail.

It's not even "dumb shit that doesn't really add much to the gameplay" that's my major criticism - often games, in particular those that are console-exclusive, are designed to push the hardware far more than can be smoothly operated, often leading to critical slowdowns, texture/model popping and (in the worst case scenarios) major game-breaking glitches that have players phase through geometry because the overtaxed hardware buckles.

Texture resolution is such a non-issue that it's easily countered by upping VRAM and RAM. I'm talking about bad industry practices that have developers leave their games bloated with badly-optimised geometry and poly counts.
